title: Candidates Race Toward Election Day
summary:
With Election Day just over a week away, candidates are working hard. Control of Congress is at stake in the midterm elections, and big names hit the campaign trail.

On Monday, President Donald Trump campaigned in Mississippi, a state he won two years ago. In Michigan, a tight Senate race will help decide which party controls the Senate. It pits Republican Mike Rogers against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who would be the nation's first Muslim senator.

Trump attacked El-Sayed's faith and said he would be a threat to national security. El-Sayed answered that the attacks were a distraction from voters' concerns about the economy. Rogers stood by his claims linking El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, though there is no evidence of a link.

Obama rallied voters in Michigan and Ohio on Saturday. He said Trump was responsible for rising costs because of the war with Iran. Obama also joked about Trump's Washington, D.C., renovation projects and all the gold.

Late Monday, a federal appeals court denied a Justice Department request to block California from counting some 20,000 mail-in ballots.
why_it_matters: Elections decide who makes rules that can affect your school, your family, and the prices your family pays.

background_read: In midterm elections, voters choose members of Congress, and the party that wins more seats gains control.
Candidates travel and speak to voters to win support, and close races in states like Michigan can help decide which party controls the Senate.
Mail-in ballots are votes sent by mail, and courts can decide rules about whether they are counted.
